AdmittedSource.description:
One row of the grant history for a source in a space.

Every grant, renewal and revocation is its own row, so this is a point in a history rather than
a mutable record. ``state`` is derived at read time: expiry is a predicate on a live row, not a
stored lifecycle value, so a grant that has simply lapsed is still the live row for its pair and
renewing it supersedes it rather than resurrecting it.

reconciliation view, which a steward reaches later or never.

ClaimWipeResponse.description:
What a whole-agent claim wipe erased.

Counts rather than receipts: a wipe writes one receipt per entity, and returning hundreds of
them inline would make the destructive call's response the largest in the API for no reader's
benefit. Every receipt is durable, and ``request_ids`` names the ones this wipe wrote.

``has_residue`` is true when any of those receipts is, so an operator sees from the wipe alone
that some run still holds an erased entity's offers.

``remaining_entities`` is what makes the call repeatable rather than open-ended: one request
erases a bounded batch, and a non-zero count is the caller's instruction to come back. It counts
the corpus after the pass, so a run that harvested a claim mid-wipe shows up here rather than
being quietly missed.

``attributes_removed`` is only ever non-zero on the pass that empties the corpus, since the
vocabulary is shared and cannot go while an entity still needs it. It reports zero if that sweep
itself failed, which understates the reach rather than overstating it.
ClaimWipeResponse.title: ClaimWipeResponse

Request to create a space.

The kind is fixed to ``domain`` server-side; the name and an optional external
registration are caller-supplied. ``registration`` is the one genuinely optional
field on this surface, and legitimately so: omitting it and sending it as null both

DeclineReason.description:
Why a turn ended with nothing worth learning.

A closed set: an unrecognised value is rejected rather than stored, so the
column stays queryable and cannot accrue junk cardinality. These mirror the
gates a host applies before shipping an episode, and they are what makes an
otherwise invisible client-side decision measurable.
DeclineReason.title: DeclineReason

DeclineRequest.description:
Close a run whose turn ended with nothing worth learning.

The terminal counterpart to observe/reinforce. A host that resolves and then
finds the turn not worth learning from must say so rather than going silent:
silence is indistinguishable from a host that broke, and that ambiguity is
what makes a loop-closure alert uninterpretable.

Declining does not add the episode to the corpus. It records the run as
closed, attributes it to a host, and settles the resolve reservation.

agent_name.description: Human-readable agent name, unique within your tenant. This is not the hosted agent UUID used in `/agents/{agent_id}` REST paths. If no agent with this name exists yet, a write-scoped call (`agents:write`) creates a minimal learning agent in your tenant. `POST /resolve` with only `agents:read` looks up an existing name and does not insert. Reuse the same name on resolve, observe, reinforce, and distill to target the same learning corpus. Clients conventionally namespace an agent-loop `run_id` as `<agent_name>:...`; if yours does, avoid the name `distill`, because `distill:` is reserved for corpus distillation run ids and every agent-loop write would be refused.
agent_name.title: Agent Name

is_delivered.description: Whether this turn's recall was delivered in a way the turn can be credited for. A turn can receive the injection and still decline, so this decides whether the resolve is billed or released: the caller is charged for the resolve this turn consumed, never for one it did not. A warm stash reports false and is not charged even though the model saw it, because the block was resolved on an earlier turn and this turn consumed no resolve of its own. Whether that earlier turn was itself charged is that turn's own report, not something this field asserts. Omitted means the host did not report either way, which is recorded as unknown rather than as a definite non-delivery: the credit alert separates a decline that lost credit from one that never had any to lose, and a default of false would silently file every omitting client under the second.
is_delivered.title: Is Delivered

reason.description: Why the turn had nothing worth learning from.

recall_outcome.description: Why the recall earned nothing this turn, from the same closed set reinforce uses. A declined turn that was never shown its learnings is a different run from one that was shown them and did too little to be worth learning from, and different again from one shown a warm stash it can never be credited for. Sending this without `is_delivered` is enough: the flag is derived from it. Sending both with different meanings is not refused, it is reconciled in favour of this field and the disagreement is logged.

run_id.description: The caller-owned `run_id` supplied to resolve; it must not start with `distill:`, which is reserved for distillation jobs.
run_id.title: Run Id

source_framework.description: Producing host/framework, used to attribute the per-host funnel. Optional; the server derives one when it is absent. `unknown` is reserved: the loop-closure funnel groups runs with no attribution under that label and excludes them from alerting, so a value equal to it is normalised to unset rather than stored as a host.
source_framework.title: Source Framework

DistillRequest.description:
Extract learnings from a corpus of evidence, without fabricating tool steps.

Use for post-mortems, documents, diffs, and analysis output. A distillation
job is standalone and does not participate in the resolve, observe, and
reinforce loop.

examples.evaluation: The useful contrast is bounded retries and a clear stop condition, not the provider-specific error text.

evidence.content: The initial response retried every failed checkout request immediately. This increased load, delayed recovery, and produced repeated alerts. Operators could not tell which retries were safe, and the runbook did not define a stop condition.
evidence.label: Initial response

evidence.content: The revised response honoured retry hints, applied bounded backoff with jitter, and stopped automated retries when the error budget threshold was reached. Operators received one clear escalation and recovery completed without adding material load. The runbook now records ownership and the next review time.
evidence.label: Revised response

agent_name.description: Human-readable agent name, unique within your tenant. This is not the hosted agent UUID used in `/agents/{agent_id}` REST paths. If no agent with this name exists yet, a write-scoped call (`agents:write`) creates a minimal learning agent in your tenant. `POST /resolve` with only `agents:read` looks up an existing name and does not insert. Reuse the same name on resolve, observe, reinforce, and distill to target the same learning corpus. Clients conventionally namespace an agent-loop `run_id` as `<agent_name>:...`; if yours does, avoid the name `distill`, because `distill:` is reserved for corpus distillation run ids and every agent-loop write would be refused.
agent_name.title: Agent Name

evaluation.description: Reviewer verdict or contrast aid; folded into the grounding corpus.

max_learnings.description: Maximum number of learnings to extract from this distill job. Defaults to 10; lower for sparse corpora or raise for large, dense documents.
max_learnings.title: Max Learnings

occurred_at.description: RFC 3339 time the corpus was produced. It stamps the learnings so they decay from the real time rather than from ingestion, and it anchors any obligation harvested from the corpus, so a relative deadline ('by Friday', 'end of next week') resolves against the week the writer was in rather than the week we received it. Carry the offset: a date-only deadline belongs to a calendar day in the writer's own zone, and a bare UTC timestamp reads it in ours. An item that declares its own `declared_sensitivity.provenance.source_time` uses that instead, for that item. A timestamp's zero value (the Unix epoch, or the first instant of year 1) is refused here and on an item's `source_time` as an unset field: omit it when the time is unknown.
occurred_at.title: Occurred At

DocumentCitationRequest.description:
The span of a stored document this evidence was drawn from.

**All six members or none, and that is enforced by them being required here rather than
checked later.** Core's `citation_pointer` returns a pointer only when all six survived
admission, because five of six is a span with no end, or an end with no document, and
resolving one would mean inventing the missing member. A model where each was optional would
let a caller send five, have it silently ignored, and be told nothing.

`doc_id` is bounded in BYTES, from the store's own bound, and is NOT stripped. Both are the
store's rules rather than choices made here: the key is the caller's identity for the
document, so trimming it would silently make two of their documents one, and a character bound
against a byte store lets a multibyte key mint a pointer to a document that can never exist.

The other five rules the store enforces on a document key (no `..`, no leading separator, no
empty segment, no backslash, no control character) are NOT re-derived here. A check that
duplicates another component's rule and gets a fraction of it is worse than no check, because
it reads as one; the service layer calls the store's own `validate_doc_id` on the way through.

doc_id.description: The customer's own key for the document this passage lives in. Bounded in bytes to match the document store, and kept exactly as sent: two keys differing only by whitespace are two different documents.
doc_id.title: Doc Id

end.description: Character offset the span ends at.
end.title: End

segmenter_version.description: Part of the pointer rather than metadata about it, because it is part of the unit's identity: the same text segmented by a different version is different units.
segmenter_version.title: Segmenter Version

start.description: Character offset the span starts at.
start.title: Start

text_sha256.description: The normalised text version the span is an offset into.
text_sha256.title: Text Sha256

unit_index.description: Which unit of that text version.
unit_index.title: Unit Index

A client that stages a turn and flushes it later must send this, or "by Friday" resolves against the flush and lands on the wrong day. EvidenceItemModel.description:
One piece of corpus evidence to distill learnings from.

Supply primary text plus a light label and role so contrasting items can be
compared, such as a baseline and fix or a failure and success.

channel.description: Required. How this item reached you, stated by the sender and never guessed. A chat message states `chat`; the pages name a chat message by its thread only when this says so. Send `unknown` when you do not know.

content.description: Primary text; the grounding source extraction quotes from.
content.title: Content

declared_sensitivity.description: Optional caller-declared metadata for this item, in the same vocabulary as a step's. Nest these members under a `provenance` key, e.g. `{"provenance": {"source_id": "...", "genre": "..."}}`; a flat top-level `source_id` (or `genre`, `author`, `source_time`, `source_class`) is refused rather than silently read as no declaration. How the item reached you is the item's own `channel` field above, never a member of this record: a `channel` here, nested or flat, is refused. The record may also carry a citation into a stored document: `doc_id`, `text_sha256` and `segmenter_version` as strings, and `unit_index`, `start` and `end` as INTEGERS, naming the exact passage this item's evidence was drawn from. A numeric string for an offset is refused deliberately, because it is a second shape for the same pointer. `attacker_reachable` is a BOOLEAN: `true` says someone outside your organisation can write into this source, and holds what is read from it as untrusted. `false` is ignored, because a source vouching for itself is not believed. The `provenance` record says where the item came from: `genre` is what kind of artefact it is (policy, plan, minutes, reference, correspondence, note, aside) and conditions how authoritative it is, while the item's `channel` says how it reached you and conditions how fast it goes stale. A signed policy pasted into a chat thread is both, which is why they are separate. Also `source_id`, `author`, and an RFC 3339 `source_time` for when the facts in it became true. An unrecognised `genre` is kept verbatim and left unranked rather than refused. `source_class` is the superseded single-facet form, still accepted and never ranked. To say what the item is *about*, use the `subject` field above rather than this record.
declared_sensitivity.title: Declared Sensitivity

identity_markers.description: Optional caller hints for people in this item: fuller names, emails, or Slack ids. Must appear verbatim in content or they are dropped. Distill also harvests those forms automatically when they sit next to the name.
identity_markers.title: Identity Markers

obligations.description: Typed obligations this item already carries, written verbatim with no LLM involved: they are stored directly on the obligation shelf as provenance_class=user_directed and never enter this item's extraction. A relative due phrase ('next Friday') is refused at request validation rather than resolved; pre-resolve it before sending. Up to 8 per item, 50 across a request. Each obligation's own outcome (written, deduped, or a refusal) is reported on GET /learning-runs/{run_id}/status, not on the 202 this request returns.
obligations.title: Obligations

record_context.description:
What your connector knows about the document this item came from: which accounts it belongs to, who was on it, and what it answers. A declaration, and the only rung that can reach a document whose text names no account.

Sent as its own typed field rather than inside `declared_sensitivity`, so the shapes are in this schema and a malformed one is a 422 naming the field rather than a value accepted and dropped later. A `record_context` key inside `declared_sensitivity` is ignored, for the same reason `subject` is: one concept, one way to declare it.

It is checked by the runtime's own rules at this door, and it needs a `source_ref` or an identifier to be filed under; one with neither is refused.

source_ref.description: Non-secret provenance: a doc id or URL. This is the input that decides whether a claim distilled from this item can name where it came from. A claim grounded in a passage of this item carries this string back as its citation's `grounding_ref`, so a later question read answers with the filename you sent. Omit it and the claim is still recorded and still returned, but with `citation_absence: source_undeclared` instead of a citation, and the name cannot be recovered afterwards because it was never sent. Send it whenever the item has a source, even a rough one.
source_ref.title: Source Ref

source_url.description: Where your own system shows the document this item came from, an absolute http or https URL. An answer that cites the stored document links its source line here. Any `user:password@` is removed before it is stored; the query string is kept.
source_url.title: Source Url

subject.description: The entity this item is about, e.g. an account or product name. Given, it is the name **every** fact from this item is filed under: it outranks the entity extraction reads out of the prose, so a fact about a person named inside the item is filed under this subject too. That is what stops one entity fragmenting across two spellings and never accumulating corroboration, and it is why the field suits an item your connector already knows is about exactly one thing, such as an account note matched to a CRM record. Omit it for an item covering several entities, a meeting transcript most of all, and each fact resolves its own entity from the prose. Sending the item's title here files the whole meeting under the meeting. To say where an item came from rather than what it is about, use `source_ref` or the provenance record.
subject.title: Subject

EvidenceObligationModel.description:
A typed obligation carried on a ``/distill`` evidence item, written with no LLM involved.

The typed sibling of ``StoreObligationRequest``: the same fields, and ``extra="forbid"`` from
birth rather than added after two malformed production bodies were accepted, which is how
that model came by its own. Reuses ``ObligationDueModel`` and
``ObligationPartyModel`` verbatim, which is what makes relative-date refusal free: ``due.at``
is a typed, aware-only ``datetime`` and this path has no phrase parser, so a relative date
such as "next Friday" fails Pydantic coercion before any obligation logic runs, where the
harvest lane deliberately resolves one against the note's own anchor.

ParticipantModel.description:
One person or resource on the document.

**Send the address as `email`.** On the learning boundary we never store it; a document sent to the documents API keeps the address with that document and erases it with the document (a blind copy recipient is never kept). The platform turns it into a keyed
pseudonym under a secret only your tenant's keys hold, keeps the registrable domain, and drops
the address before anything is queued or stored. The same person in two meetings is then one
person before either transcript is read. There is no field for a key of your own: a key a
sender could choose could be aimed at somebody else.

email.description: The participant's address, bare (`dave@northwindclinics.example`). Split at the platform into a keyed pseudonym and a registrable domain; the runtime never receives it. The learning boundary drops it there; the documents API keeps it with the document, to show on the document's own page, and erases it with the document. One that is not a bare address is refused.

email_authentication.description: What your mail system found when it checked this sender (SPF, DKIM or DMARC): `passed`, `failed` or `not_checked`. A `from` participant counts as one of your own people only when `is_internal` is true and this is `passed`, because a forged address is how a payment instruction is faked. Leave it out when you have no result, and the sender is read as an outside party.

name.description: The participant's display name. An address sent here (`dave@northwindclinics.example`, or `Dave Smith <dave@northwindclinics.example>`) is taken as the email when none is sent, and only the display part is kept.

RecallOutcome.description:
What became of a run's recall, as the client that owns the loop observed it.

A run that credits nothing has one signature at this boundary, an absent receipt,
and three causes that license different responses. The recall never reached the
model, in which case there is nothing to vouch for and the client is correct. It was
shown and the record of it could not be read back, which is a wiring defect. Or what
the model saw was a warm stash carried over from an earlier turn of the same project,
which was genuinely shown and can never be credited, because it was resolved against
a different goal and carries no run marker for a receipt to match. The receipt alone
cannot tell the three apart, so the client says which.

A closed set, like ``DeclineReason``: an unrecognised value is rejected rather than
stored, so the column stays queryable and cannot accrue junk cardinality. It is the
same set the client declares in ``hyperstruck/ide/recall.py``, and a member the
client can send and this one cannot costs that run its whole episode rather than
merely its diagnostic, because the request model forbids an unknown value. A new
member lands here first.
RecallOutcome.title: RecallOutcome

Surfaced rather than silent, because a short list would read identically to a source that was never observed, which is the single inference this view exists to make safe. A further page is next_cursor, not this.
is_truncated.title: Is Truncated

next_cursor.description: Present when another page follows. Ordinary paging, and deliberately not the same thing as the truncation flag below.
next_cursor.title: Next Cursor

unlistable_source_count.description: Declared sources this view refuses to list because their id is longer than a grant may ever be. They are reported as a count rather than dropped in silence: such an id is a source arriving with no grant and no way to make one, and the caller supplying the corpus chooses it.
unlistable_source_count.title: Unlistable Source Count

unreachable_grant_count.description: Live grants in this tenant stored under a space id no lookup can produce, so they match nothing, cannot be revoked through the API (revocation resolves the same projection and addresses a different row) and are absent from the items above. A commons space is addressed by the slug and never by its row uuid; a grant written the other way is inert, as are a grant on a uuid naming no space and a grant on a misspelt slug, and all three are counted. Counted rather than listed because the cure is a direct write. **Null means not measured**, which a truncated scan and every page after the first both are: it is tenant-wide, so it is read once per walk rather than per page, and zero would say 'no unreachable grants', which is the opposite answer. Reported at all because this view could previously see every grant EXCEPT the ones it exists to find. On 2026-09-07 one such row cost 516 claims their channel trust.
unreachable_grant_count.title: Unreachable Grant Count

unscoped_document_count.description: Notes in this tenant that declared a source and carry no space at all. They are invisible to the observed side, because equality never matches null, so a non-zero count here is why a grant may report as never observed while its notes are being read. It is the difference between 'this source was never seen' and 'nothing here is space-scoped yet'.
unscoped_document_count.title: Unscoped Document Count

RecordContextModel.description:
What your connector already knows about the document this item came from.

A DECLARATION, NOT AN INFERENCE, and it is the primary way a document reaches its account. The
inference rungs read the prose, so a ticket, a calendar invite or a CRM export whose text names
no account reaches none of them however good they get.

A RESEND REPLACES THIS DOCUMENT'S SET rather than merging into it, keyed on the `source_ref`
you sent with the item. A participant dropped from a corrected invite and a container moved to
another account are retracted by the write itself, so send the whole context each time rather
than a delta.

Every member is refused rather than trimmed when it is malformed, and the refusal names the
field: a sender learns their payload was wrong instead of discovering months later that half of
it had been silently dropped.

A timestamp's zero value (the Unix epoch, or the first instant of year 1) is refused as an unset field: omit the field when the time is unknown.
occurred_at.title: Occurred At

agent_name.description: Human-readable agent name, unique within your tenant. This is not the hosted agent UUID used in `/agents/{agent_id}` REST paths. If no agent with this name exists yet, a write-scoped call (`agents:write`) creates a minimal learning agent in your tenant. `POST /resolve` with only `agents:read` looks up an existing name and does not insert. Reuse the same name on resolve, observe, reinforce, and distill to target the same learning corpus. Clients conventionally namespace an agent-loop `run_id` as `<agent_name>:...`; if yours does, avoid the name `distill`, because `distill:` is reserved for corpus distillation run ids and every agent-loop write would be refused.
agent_name.title: Agent Name

context_receipt.description: The host's record of the context block as its editor accepted it, used to confirm which offered learnings the model was actually shown. A learning no receipt reports as rendered credits nothing, so a host that omits this earns no reinforcement. Send the artefact the editor produced, never the text this client emitted: an echo of what was sent asserts the very thing the receipt exists to evidence. An over-cap receipt is clipped when folded rather than refused, because refusing it would cost the run its whole reinforcement and not merely its evidence; the bound on this field is far above that clip and exists only to stop an unbounded body.
context_receipt.title: Context Receipt

episode.description: Completed episode using the same caller-owned `run_id` supplied to resolve.

is_delivered.description: Whether this turn's recall was delivered in a way the turn can be credited for, which is not the same question as whether the model saw something. Omit it and an absent `context_receipt` has two readings, a run that was shown its learnings and lost the evidence and a run that was never shown them at all, and only the first is a defect. A warm stash is the case where the two readings come apart: it was shown, and it reports false here, because it carries no run marker any receipt could match. NULL means the client did not say.
is_delivered.title: Is Delivered

is_org_promotion_allowed.description: Whether eligible learnings may be considered for organisation sharing.
is_org_promotion_allowed.title: Is Org Promotion Allowed

recall_outcome.description: Why the recall produced no receipt this turn, from a closed set. Distinguishes a resolve that timed out or failed, a stash no tool event ever showed, a warm stash that WAS shown and can never be credited, and a transcript whose format the client no longer recognises, which is the one that silently ends the whole credit path. Not every member means the model saw nothing: `stash_emitted` means it saw an earlier turn's block. Sending this without `is_delivered` is enough: the flag is derived from it. Sending both with different meanings is not refused, it is reconciled in favour of this field, which is the more specific of the two, and the disagreement is logged.

test_run.description: Whether this run is a test run. Omit it: the mark set at resolve applies. Stating a value that contradicts the mark set at resolve is refused with 409 `test_run_mismatch`. A run that was never resolved takes this value, defaulting to false.
test_run.title: Test Run

value.description: Value this run produced, recorded on the agent's value ledger and credited to the learnings and claims the run was offered. Send `unit_key` and `quantity` from the agent's rate card, `amount_usd` with a `baseline`, or `time_saved_minutes`. A block that does not match this schema is refused with 422 like any other field. Once accepted, it is recorded only when the agent tracks value and the caller can write to the agent; the outcome is reported as `value_status` and never fails the run close. Record value only when this agent's value tracking is on and you have a basis you did not invent: a rate-card unit that matches what happened, or a figure a person, a document or a system of record stated. Never guess a dollar figure; the platform writes its own estimate after successful runs.

ResolveFactLane.description:
Why the claims block holds what it holds, so an empty one is read correctly.

An empty block has causes that call for opposite actions: the goal named an entity the account
holds no claim about, the goal named no entity the account holds, the agent's documents are
still being replayed, the tool resolve asked for none, or the recall failed. Only the first is
a statement about the account.

is_complete.description: Whether the block holds everything the account holds for this goal. False on any outcome that cut or abandoned work, so a measurement does not use it as the denominator.
is_complete.title: Is Complete

is_degraded.description: Whether the lane could not run, as opposed to running and finding nothing. True is an operational state on our side, not a statement about the account.
is_degraded.title: Is Degraded

outcome.description: bound (the block holds the claims about the entities the goal names), bound_partial (the block's budget cut some claims), no_match (the goal names an entity the account holds and the account holds no live claim about it), no_entity_named (the goal names no entity the account holds, so nothing was looked up; the account may still hold claims the goal describes, which an answer finds), suppressed (a tool's first-use resolve carries no claims), not_replayed (the agent's documents are still being replayed into the claim store) or failed (the recall could not run). 'no_match' is the only one meaning the account holds nothing for this goal.
outcome.title: Outcome

ResolveResponse.description:
What this run was offered: two separately placeable blocks and the ids behind them.

``injected_text`` carries the advice half (rules, plus the annotations compiled from
proceduralised learnings). ``injected_facts_text`` carries the fenced block of claims the account
holds about the entities the goal names, open obligations among them, on its own so a host can
place it where its model reads it best and keep the more stable advice half in a cached prompt
prefix. ``offered_claim_ids`` are the claims that block renders.

``fact_lane`` says why the claims block is what it is, on every resolve. It is typed optional so
a client reading an older deployment's response does not fail on its absence; absent means
unknown, never fine.

claims.description: The keys `injected_facts_text` renders, as Claim items, for a host that renders them under its own design. Null when nothing was recalled; never an empty list.

fact_lane.description: Why the claims block holds what it holds. Present on every resolve. Read it before concluding from an empty `offered_claim_ids` that the account holds nothing: only outcome 'no_match' means that.

has_reported_outcomes.description: True once this agent's host has reported the outcome of any run through reinforce. A learning is recommended only after it has helped in two runs, and only a reported outcome can say it helped, so while this is false nothing can be recommended and the advice block ends with a sentence saying so.
has_reported_outcomes.title: Has Reported Outcomes

is_all_offered.description: True when this resolve returned nothing because everything relevant to the goal had already been offered in the request's session window. Distinct from a corpus with nothing relevant, which leaves it false.
is_all_offered.title: Is All Offered

learnings.description: The offered learnings' evidence as data, mirroring the `Source:` line in `injected_text` without our prose. Null when no learning was offered; never an empty list.

owed_rule.description: How to decide the owed items listed in `claims` with `evidence`: DO, SKIP or CHECK. Present whenever one is.

documents.description: On a run whose items were stored as documents, one entry per evidence item in request order: the document it became (`doc_id`, `version`) and its `outcome`: `queued` while its ingest is pending, then `stored` (a new document), `new_version` (changed text under an existing document), `unchanged` (identical text already stored, so nothing was read again), `refused` with a `reason`, or `failed`. items.description: What the reader did with each item you sent, one entry each. Null until the job finishes, and null on a run finished under a Core older than the reader; empty on a run that carried no corpus. obligation_outcomes.description: What became of each typed obligation this run's evidence carried, one entry per obligation submitted. obligations_written.description: Owed claims stated in the prose this run ingested: what someone is to do. Counts the corpus lane only: the agent's own answer is reported separately as own_output_obligations_written, because one number moved by two lanes with different triggers cannot be attributed to either.

own_output_obligations_written.description: Obligations this run harvested from the answer the agent itself composed, written to the shelf held for review. declared_sensitivity.description: Optional caller-declared metadata for this step. Sections whose value is a mapping carry per-field declarations (`args`, `result`, `result_attributes`, `result_integrity`, and the `provenance` record). Sections whose value is a string carry a single declaration, of which `subject` is the one the runtime reads: the argument key naming the entity this step's result is about. A provenance member (`source_id`, `channel`, `genre`, `author`, `source_time`, `source_class`) declared at the top level instead of nested under `provenance` is refused, because a flat one is read as no declaration at all rather than as a second home for the same fact. The `provenance` record may also carry a citation into a stored document: `doc_id`, `text_sha256` and `segmenter_version` as strings, and `unit_index`, `start` and `end` as INTEGERS. Those six travel together and name the exact passage this step's evidence was drawn from, so a learning built from it can be resolved back to the text it rests on. The offsets must be integers: a numeric string is refused deliberately, because it is a second shape for the same pointer. `attacker_reachable` is a BOOLEAN: `true` says someone outside your organisation can write into this source, and holds what is read from it as untrusted. `false` is ignored, because a source vouching for itself is not believed, and any other shape is dropped.

UpdateSpaceRegistrationRequest.description:
Register or re-point the external container a space mirrors.

``registration`` is required and never null. This body cannot clear a registration:
clearing is ``DELETE`` on the same subresource, which needs no body at all and so
needs nothing from a client that a generated client might not be able to send.

That split also settles a conflict the flat model papered over. One model serves both
a ``PUT`` and a ``PATCH``, where an absent field should mean "clear" for the former
and "unchanged" for the latter. Making absence an error in both sidestepped the
question at runtime, in a way the published schema could not express. A single
required member has no absent case for the two verbs to disagree about.

registration.description: The external container this space mirrors. Required: send `DELETE` to this same path to unregister the space.

ZeroYieldReason.description:
Why a finished job produced nothing on a shelf.

A closed set rather than free text, because the whole point of reporting a zero is that a
client can branch on it: retry with more evidence, correct a declaration, or accept that the
corpus held nothing new. A value outside this set is a defect, never a passthrough.

``WEAK_CONTRAST`` is the one that used to be a 400. Contrast is what the *learning* extractor
compares against, so a corpus that declares none can still be full of facts; refusing it at the
door refused the claim shelf along with the rule shelf. It is now advice attached to the
result, which is the same guidance arriving after the job rather than instead of it.
ZeroYieldReason.title: ZeroYieldReason

post.description: Searches the agent's claims for the ones nearest the question and renders them by code under one line saying so, each paragraph opened by its entity and attribute, with the same claims beside the text as items, so the same question gets the same result. The claims are the nearest the account holds and may not answer the question; whether one answers is the caller's to judge. Compose from what is handed over first and narrow only after. `shares_no_word` is true when no claim shares a word with the question, so the claims are the nearest by meaning alone, and `more_matched` counts the claims the question's words matched beyond those handed over. Each item's `word_share` and `cosine` say how much of the question's words it carries and how near it is in meaning. Only an account or entity holding no live claim gets `shape: absent`. When the search by meaning is unavailable the result says `degraded: embedding_unavailable` or `degraded: vectors_loading` and ranks by words alone; `vectors_loading` is said only when an account's copies failed to load or were dropped as out of date. Each deploy empties the copies the search by meaning reads, so after a deploy an account's first question waits for its signs to load (about a second at 500,000 claims) and ranks by them until the numbers arrive (a few seconds more). `entity` narrows the search to one entity's claims (404 when the account does not hold it). With any of `state`, `kind`, `owner` or `due_before` the result is `shape: set`: the claims GET /claims would list for that filter, one row each under a line stating the filter, paged by `cursor` and `limit`; the question is not ranked. A safe read: nothing is written or billed, so a retry needs no Idempotency-Key. Returns 409 `claims_not_replayed` until the agent's claims have been rebuilt on the keyed store.

delete.description: Destroys the wrapped data keys first, so from that instant every copy they protect is unreadable whether or not the deletes that follow complete, and returns a receipt naming what each scope actually reached. Any queued or running ingest for this document is cancelled: a deletion request is the one operation that must never queue behind other work. The learnings distilled from the document are reported in two scopes: `learnings` counts those deleted because only this document supported them, and `learning_citations` counts those kept on their other sources with this document removed. Either scope reads `not_tracked` when the document was only distilled before learnings recorded their source, and `deleted_incomplete` when only some of its distillations were, so a zero is never reported for learnings the erasure could not have found. The id of a run the claim store holds a record of is erased too, in any space of the agent: its kept text goes, its queued reading is cancelled, every other claim-store record of the run is erased, and the receipt counts the claims and citations the run filed that were removed. It reads incomplete while a reading of the run is in flight. The episode's plan record, with the goal and step text, is not touched by this route: the episode erasure removes it.

put.description:
Store one submission under the caller's own document key and queue it for ingest. Returns 202 with the new version when work was enqueued, and 200 with the existing version when identical bytes are already stored: a 202 on a duplicate would promise work that will not happen. Refuses 409 when the tenant has no document key binding, 413 above the configured size ceiling, and 404 for an unknown agent, in each case without enqueueing anything.

Send `multipart/form-data` with a `content` part and a `metadata` part: JSON carrying the compulsory `channel` (`unknown` when you do not know how the document reached you), and optionally `title`, `occurred_at` and a `record_context` in `/distill`'s schema. The metadata is what links the document to its account and dates it, and the claims read from the document carry both. A `source_url` is the link an answer citing the document shows. Bytes identical to a stored version are not read again: their metadata fills a `title`, `source_url`, `occurred_at` or `channel` the stored version lacks (a stored `unknown` channel counts as lacking), and never replaces one it has, except that a held `occurred_at` without a real offset (`+00:00`) takes the same instant stated with one; a stated `occurred_at` later than the arrival of the earliest stored version of the same text is not filled, and a time that is filled lands on that version. A title declared this way does replace one derived from the document's own pages, in the answers that cite it.

get.description: One item per value the learning renders from a claim instead of a fixed literal, in the learning's order: the claim the value was distilled from and whether it still stands, and the claim its slot resolves to now with the value recall would render. A value recall would not offer (in conflict, or of untrusted or unknown origin) carries its state and no text. A safety rule keeps rendering the value it was written with when its slot now holds a different one, so that item shows the earlier value with `is_held_for_safety` true. When the claim store cannot be read the list answers with `is_degraded` true and every value `unresolved`. `status` keeps the values whose resolved claim is in that state. A learning with no such values is a 200 with no items. A cursor from an earlier release answers 400 `cursor_invalid`. A protected value (a bank account number) reads `Ends 5560` unless the caller holds `claims:curate`, has the right to change the agent, and sends `reveal=true`.

post.description: Distill durable learnings from post-mortems, documents, diffs, or analysis without inventing tool steps. Supply ``agent_name`` (your agent's human-readable name, not the hosted UUID from `/agents/{agent_id}`). If no agent with that name exists yet, one is created automatically on first use within your tenant. Creating a new name requires `agents:write`. Submit at least 1 evidence item. A request body is capped at 26 MiB, and there is no item count or corpus total. Each item becomes a document of the agent (keyed on its first `record_context.identifiers` entry as `scheme:value`, else its `source_ref`, else a hash of its text), claims cite the passage they came from, and a resend of identical text costs nothing. A corpus that declares no contrast is accepted rather than refused: contrast is what the learning extractor compares against, so a corpus without it can still be full of facts, and a run that yields nothing for that reason comes back as `zero_reason: weak_contrast` on `GET /learning-runs/{run_id}/status`, where a count stays null until the job finishes, which is not the same as zero. `run_id` is a caller-created idempotency and tracing value, must begin with `distill:`, and is never looked up as a resource. A valid request may yield no learning. Pre-redact secrets from evidence.

Narrowed to the reinforced-retention interval when it exceeds it, because past that boundary closed runs have been reclaimed while unclosed ones survive; the response reports the window actually used, and reports rates as null when that narrowing leaves the window below the same ratio.

POST and PATCH install pending `starter_key` eval nodes in the save transaction; 422 `eval_output_differs` when the tenant's eval of that name has a different output.

post.description: Validates the input against the workflow's schema (422 with `/input/<field>` pointers, no run created), holds the run's estimated cost against the spend cap (403 `spend_limit`), then runs it in the background. With `wait_seconds` (up to 60) the request waits: 200 with the run once it succeeds, or the run's error mapped to a status (502 model failed, 503 evaluator unavailable, 409 evaluator incompatible or cancelled, 504 timed out). Otherwise, or when the wait ends first, 202 with the run id to poll. A workflow with an insight node also needs `claims:read` and read access to every agent its insight rule names. `trigger_kind` comes from how the request authenticated: `portal`, `api` or `mcp`.

tags.description: Use these endpoints to inspect the identity and tenant selected by a Hyperstruck portal session. API-key integrations normally use the resource endpoints directly.
tags.name: auth

tags.description: Use these endpoints to discover the authenticated caller's plan and granted capabilities before enabling optional integration features.
tags.name: entitlements

tags.description: Use these endpoints to create, configure, discover, and manage hosted agents, or to start work for a specific agent.
tags.name: agents

tags.description: Use these endpoints to track the lifetime value an agent produces: turn tracking on with a rate card of priced outcomes, record value when an outcome happens, reverse an entry that turned out wrong, and read totals that keep measured and estimated value apart. Each profile carries `guidance` telling an agent how to record value for that agent.
tags.name: agent_value

tags.description: Use these portal-session endpoints to create, list, and revoke tenant API keys used by server-to-server integrations.
tags.name: api_keys

tags.description: Use these endpoints to store, search, inspect, curate, and remove the durable learnings associated with a hosted agent.
tags.name: learnings

tags.description: Use these endpoints to inspect learnings shared across the caller's organisation. This surface is intended for tenant-wide discovery.
tags.name: org_learnings

tags.description: Use this portal-session endpoint to list active organization members for invite pickers (identity only; available to any org member).
tags.name: org_directory

tags.description: Use these portal-session, admin/owner-only endpoints to list the caller's organization members and change member roles.
tags.name: org_members

tags.description: Use these portal-session endpoints to record that a declared corpus source is trusted within one space, so facts harvested from it are no longer held for review on arrival. Grants expire and are renewed rather than standing forever, every grant, renewal and withdrawal is kept, and the reconciliation endpoint shows the sources your facts actually declare against the grants you have made.
tags.name: space_admitted_sources

tags.description: Use these portal-session endpoints to create or delete domain spaces in the caller's organization, and to invite, list, or revoke direct space members.
tags.name: org_spaces

tags.description: Use these framework-neutral endpoints to retrieve learnings before external work, submit completed experience, or extract learnings from a corpus. Identifiers in these request bodies are caller-managed.
tags.name: learning_boundary

tags.description: Use these read-only endpoints to find prior plans relevant to a new goal for one or more accessible agents.
tags.name: plans

tags.description: Use these endpoints to start, inspect, list, and resume hosted agent runs. Hosted run identifiers are server-issued UUIDs.
tags.name: runs

tags.description: Use these endpoints to read conversation sessions, including their messages and associated hosted runs.
tags.name: sessions

tags.description: Use these endpoints to discover the spaces the authenticated caller can access when selecting an agent home or filtering resources.
tags.name: spaces

tags.description: Use these endpoints to report metered activity, inspect recent run usage, and understand usage attributed to the calling tenant.
tags.name: usage

tags.description: Use these endpoints to manage space-scoped success-metric defaults, reusable charts, multi-chart dashboards, and Mode B aggregated queries over daily reporting facts.
tags.name: reporting

tags.description: Use these endpoints to define standing insight rules over your agents, run them, follow each run's steps, and act on the cited findings they produce. Available when Insights is enabled for your tenant.
tags.name: insights

tags.description: Use these endpoints to define reusable evals (what is judged and the shape of the answer: a choice, a score or a yes/no probability), list the evaluators that can judge them, install a starter eval, and try one eval on a single input. Available when Evals is enabled for your tenant.
tags.name: evals

tags.description: Use these endpoints to define a workflow (a trigger, an optional insight, eval steps and an answer), run it by API with a bounded synchronous wait, follow a run's steps, list runs by date range, and record corrections. Available when Workflows is enabled for your tenant.
tags.name: workflows

tags.description: Use these endpoints to inspect the tenant's current spend-limit and billing-window summary.
tags.name: billing

tags.description: Use these endpoints to review, promote, release, and administer claims for hosted agents, and to inspect organization-wide claim queues such as quarantine, abstained, and split proposals.
tags.name: claims

tags.description: Use these endpoints to schedule a public HTTPS watch, preview the compiled crawl, enqueue a run, and inspect run history. Pages become documents through the existing document door. A 202 means accepted, not searchable yet. Cadence cannot be faster than 15 minutes.
tags.name: ingest_sources

tags.description: Use these endpoints to submit documents an agent may cite, to read what happened to one, to turn a citation back into the passage it points at, and to erase a document. A submission is queued and ingested asynchronously, so the fetch reports the queue's view and the stored version's state as two separate fields. Erasure destroys the wrapping keys first and returns a receipt naming what each protected copy actually reached.
tags.name: documents
